(ESTIMATE)}\n\\label{sec:criterion}\n\nThe main measurement is that Gemma applies a stricter refusal criterion in Slovene than in English on benign items, while GaMS3 does not.\nTable~\\ref{tab:sdt} reports the signal-detection parameters from Experiment~5.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Signal-detection parameters by model and language (Experiment~5, 1,093 safe $+$ 349 harmful items, Qwen3-14B judge).}\n\\label{tab:sdt}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\n & Gemma EN & Gemma SL & GaMS3 EN & GaMS3 SL \\\\\n\\midrule\nHit rate ($H$) & 0.89 & 0.94 & 0.90 & 0.86 \\\\\nFalse-alarm rate ($F$) & 0.364 & 0.569 & 0.273 & 0.273 \\\\\n$d'$ & 1.57 & 1.39 & 1.86 & 1.68 \\\\\n$c$ & $-0.44$ & $-0.87$ & $-0.33$ & $-0.23$ \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe DiD on the criterion parameter is $+0.52$ $[0.38, 0.68]$ (95\\% CI).\nGemma's Slovene criterion is shifted by half a standard deviation relative to the GaMS3 baseline.\nThe DiD on $d'$ is $-0.003$ $[-0.33, 0.29]$, indistinguishable from zero: the asymmetry is in the threshold, not the sensitivity.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_sdt_v0.pdf}\n\\caption{Signal-detection parameters from Experiment~5 on the HARD set (1,093 benign and 349 harmful items; Slovene machine translations vs English back-translations; refusals labelled by a local Qwen3-14B judge, with partial answers coded as non-refusals). Blue bars are English prompts and orange bars are Slovene prompts, for Gemma-3-12B-IT (``Gemma~3'') and GaMS3-12B-Instruct (``GaMS3''). (a)~False-alarm rate $F$, the proportion of benign items refused, with Wilson 95\\% confidence intervals. Brackets give the paired Slovene$-$English difference and an exact McNemar test on the same items. Gemma's rate rises from 0.364 to 0.569 ($p<10^{-28}$), while GaMS3 refuses 0.273 of benign items in both languages ($p=1.0$). (b)~SDT criterion $c$ in $z$ units, where more negative means a greater tendency to refuse. Lower brackets show the within-model shift $\\Delta c$ (Slovene$-$English, 95\\% CI): Gemma moves toward refusing in Slovene ($c=-0.87$ vs $-0.44$; $\\Delta c=-0.43$ [$-0.57$, $-0.31$]), while GaMS3 does not ($-0.23$ vs $-0.33$; $\\Delta c=+0.09$ [$-0.002$, $0.19$]). The upper bracket gives the difference-in-differences $\\mathrm{DiD}_c=+0.52$ [0.38, 0.68]. The corresponding DiD on sensitivity $d'$ ($-0.003$ [$-0.33$, $0.29$]) is indistinguishable from zero, so the asymmetry lies in the threshold rather than in discrimination. This finding is rated ESTIMATE: coding partial answers as refusals reverses $\\mathrm{DiD}_c$ to $-0.31$ [$-0.62$, $-0.09$].}\n\\label{fig:sdt}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\paragraph{Rating and caveats.}\nWe use a three-level evidence rating: ROBUST (survives all pre-registered checks), ESTIMATE (the point estimate is informative but at least one sensitivity check fails), and INCONCLUSIVE (the confidence interval includes zero or the result is fragile).\nThis finding is rated ESTIMATE for three reasons.\nFirst, the sign reverses to $-0.31$ when partial answers are coded as refusals rather than compliance.\nSecond, the eval5 audit found 8 of 9 compliance-valid rows with CIs below zero, but this count was a post-hoc refinement made after the frozen rule found an unresolved cross-body disagreement.\nThird, the eval2 Qwen3-14B rescoring gives a similar interval $[0.39, 0.67]$, but this is a re-derivation from the same Experiment~5 items, not an independent sample.\n\n\\paragraph{Edited-model criterion shift.}\nOn edited models, the criterion difference disappears: Experiment~11 HARD post-edit $\\mathrm{DiD}_c = 0.14$ $[-0.78, 1.12]$, consistent with zero.\n\n\\subsection{Reply-Language Refusal (ESTIMATE, Weak Anchor)}\n\\label{sec:reply}\n\nIn the $3{\\times}3$ crossed grid (Experiment~14), edited Gemma at high dose shows a pattern in which residual refusal is higher when the model replies in Slovene than in English.\nTable~\\ref{tab:gemma_grid} gives the refusal rates.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Refusal rates at high edit dose, Gemma (harmful items, 200 per cell).}\n\\label{tab:gemma_grid}\n\\begin{tabular}{lccc}\n\\toprule\n & EN out & SL out & HU out \\\\\n\\midrule\nEN in & 0.18 & 0.77 & 0.46 \\\\\nSL in & 0.07 & 0.56 & 0.53 \\\\\nHU in & 0.10 & 0.83 & 0.55 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Refusal rates at high edit dose, GaMS3 (harmful items, 200 per cell; cells below 90\\% compliance marked $\\dag$).}\n\\label{tab:gams3_grid}\n\\begin{tabular}{lccc}\n\\toprule\n & EN out & SL out & HU out \\\\\n\\midrule\nEN in & 0.21 & 0.14 & 0.23 \\\\\nSL in & 0.16$\\dag$ & 0.15 & 0.17$\\dag$ \\\\\nHU in & 0.19$\\dag$ & 0.12$\\dag$ & 0.28 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]", "numLines": 120, "startLine": 80, "totalLines": 323}}

human review.\n\n\\paragraph{Sample size.}\nThe adjudication sample is 30 items per cell for benign false-refusal rates, limiting precision.\nThe refusal-composition numbers (54\\% explicit, 26\\% deflection) come from $n = 50$ high-dose harmful items.\n\n\\paragraph{Language compliance.}\nFour GaMS3 cells fall below 90\\% compliance (SL$\\to$EN at 0.00, HU$\\to$EN at 0.14, SL$\\to$HU at 0.56, weights.\n\n\\paragraph{Novelty.}\nThe observation that over-refusal rates differ across languages is partially anticipated by \\citet{Addagada2026} and \\citet{Nguyen2026}.\nThe present work's contribution is the signal-detection decomposition and the controlled sibling-pair design.\n\n\\section{Conclusion}\n\nUnedited Gemma-3-12B-IT false-refuses benign Slovene items at 0.569 vs 0.364 in # Over-Refusal of Benign Slovene Prompts in Gemma-3-12B Is a Criterion Shift

A 12-page research paper applying signal-detection theory (SDT) to multilingual over-refusal in safety-aligned language models. The study compares Gemma-3-12B-IT with GaMS3-12B-Instruct using controlled abliteration experiments, finding that Slovene over-refusal reflects a criterion shift (stricter decision threshold) rather than a sensitivity difference.

## Repository Layout

| File / Directory | Description |
|---|---|
| `paper.tex` | LaTeX source |
| `paper.pdf` | Compiled 12-page PDF (primary output) |
| `references.bib` | BibTeX bibliography (26 entries, each with venue or arXiv ID) |
| `references.json` | Fetch record for each bibliography entry (written by the fetch script) |
| `figures/` | Pre-generated vector figures (PDF) |
| `figures/fig_sdt_v0.pdf` | Figure 1: SDT decomposition — false-alarm rate and criterion by model and language |
| `figures/fig_grid_v0.pdf` | Figure 2: 3x3 crossed-grid refusal-rate heatmaps for Gemma and GaMS3 |
| `figures/fig_dose_v0.pdf` | Figure 3: Dose-response curves of refusal rate vs abliteration strength |

## Building the PDF

```bash
pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode paper.tex
pybtex paper.aux
pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode paper.tex
pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode paper.tex
```

Requires: `pdflatex` (TeX Live), `pybtex` (`pip install pybtex`).

## Restoring Removed Files
